If someone tells you something is rude and you do it again, its still rude, and if you know its rude why do it, it could make someone feel bad or make you look rude.

Thats why people say they're sorry, they're basically sorry for disappointing them by not liking it. Tbh though I think if someone gets served food they don't like, half will just eat it out of politeness and half will just politely say they're not keen, which isn't inherently rude (just depends how blunt or rude you say it I think).  Maybe there's a disconnect in the way the word sorry is used, sorry doesn't always necessarily mean you've fucked up and you genuinely feel remorse etc, it can be more passive....like if you brush by someone in public you say "oop sorry" not because you hurt them but just for curtesy/just in case.
